title: Codebook wording review: Each activity on a page (part 1 of 3)
background:
Review round 4 of the codebook wording. You chose on 30 October that agents draft the missing value definitions and you review every wording slot here. This page covers **each activity on a page**, part 1 of 3.

Each card is one codebook item. Open "Show the wording slots" to read them. Each slot is labelled with where its text came from:

- **Plan text**
- **New agent draft (round 4)**
- **Option text you chose in round 3**
- **Agent edit of the signed questionnaire**
- **Text you approved on 30 October**
- **Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete**

Answer per item: approve all, approve with line-edits or deletions in the comments (by slot number), or ask for a redraft. Deletion is open only for old version-2.5 slots and for one slot of each overlap pair. The batch card at the top approves everything you leave unmarked. No recommendation is given on any wording.

New agent drafts carry a certainty mark; those marked **Needs your decision** rest on no ruling or text for some point.

items.title: activity relation within page
items.situation:
Question: The extractor proposes spans; jev answers per span: new distinct activity / same as span k / component of span k / not an activity.

Recorded per activity.

14 slots: 2 × plan text; 9 × new agent draft (round 4); 3 × option text you chose in round 3.
items.body:
**1. Question** — Plan text, from review round 1
The extractor proposes spans; jev answers per span: new distinct activity / same as span k / component of span k / not an activity.

**2. Value `same_activity`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two passages describe the same activity: the same action by the same actor on the same tool or instrument.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**3. Value `component_of_program`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first passage's activity is a named component of the program described in the second. Both stay separate activities, linked.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**4. Value `has_component`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first passage describes a program, and the second passage's activity is one of its named components. Both stay separate activities, linked.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**5. Value `shared_participation`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two passages describe one joint action in which several bodies take part.
_Draft certainty: low._ **Needs your decision:** No text defines this link or says whether it merges the two passages. Please word it and say whether it merges. _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**6. Value `governs`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first passage's activity is a policy or other governance instrument that sets rules for the activity in the second (for example a policy and a tool it approves). When a pair fits both this link and a component link, this link is used.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**7. Value `governed_by`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The second passage's activity is a policy or other governance instrument that sets rules for the activity in the first. When a pair fits both this link and a component link, this link is used.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**8. Value `distinct_action`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two passages describe different activities, and none of the other links applies.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**9. Value `unresolved`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The page does not settle whether the two passages describe the same activity or different ones. They are kept separate.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**10. Value `not_an_activity`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The passage does not describe an activity as the activity rule defines one.
_Draft certainty: low._ **Needs your decision:** Links are now coded per pair of passages (activity-18 b), but this value describes one passage. Please say how it is used in a pair (for example: either passage is not an activity). _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first passage, second passage); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which passage is 'first'._

**11. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
One shared relation list serves within-page and cross-page links: same activity, component of program, has component, shared participation, governs, governed by, distinct (`distinct_action`), unresolved, plus not-an-activity within a page (r2#22; activity-16 b; all-11).

**12. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Add "has component" and "governed by".

**13. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Components stay separate activities; a governing policy is recorded as governing.

**14. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Each pair of passages gets a link.

items.title: observed actor relationship
items.situation:
Recorded per activity.

21 slots: 10 × new agent draft (round 4); 4 × text you approved on 30 October; 3 × plan text; 3 × option text you chose in round 3; 1 × agent edit of the signed questionnaire.
items.body:
**1. Relationship value `this_institution`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The searched institution itself carries out or adopts the activity.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**2. Relationship value `unit_of_institution`** — New agent draft (round 4)
An organisational unit of the searched institution (a department, office or service) carries out the activity; it counts for the institution.
_Draft certainty: high._

**3. Relationship value `joint_participant`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The activity is a joint one, and the page names the searched institution as a participant.
_Draft certainty: high._

**4. Relationship value `other`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The activity belongs to another body: a parent, sibling or neighbouring body, a separate court, board or authority, a similarly named organisation, or a vendor. The searched institution's role is still asked.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**5. Relationship value `unresolved`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The page does not settle whose activity this is. The role of the searched institution is not asked.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**6. Role value `contracting_authority`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The searched institution buys or contracts for the tool or service in its own name.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: The procurement schema gives the codes but no definition; this gloss is the ordinary procurement meaning._

**7. Role value `beneficiary`** — New agent draft (round 4)
Another body runs or buys the activity for the searched institution, and the page names the searched institution as benefiting.
_Draft certainty: high._

**8. Role value `central_purchasing_body`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The searched institution buys or sets up a contract or framework on behalf of other bodies.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**9. Role value `unit`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The searched institution takes part as a unit of the body that carries out the activity.
_Draft certainty: low._ **Needs your decision:** No text defines the roles 'unit' and 'joint'. They also repeat the relationship values 'unit of institution' and 'joint participant' (the overlap round 3 noted). Please say what each adds, or drop them.

**10. Role value `joint`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The searched institution takes part as one of several joint participants.
_Draft certainty: low._ **Needs your decision:** See 'unit': undefined and overlaps the relationship value 'joint participant'.

**11. When the role is asked** — Text you approved on 30 October
the role is asked when the relationship is `other`; skipped only when `unresolved`

**12. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
RC-D-002 row 7: the observed-actor relationship is coded per activity, not per page, with a QC flag on `confirms_activity` pages that have no own / unit / joint activity; the attribution role becomes the second of two linked parts of that relationship (relationship; role of the searched institution, "not asked" when the relationship is unresolved), describes only the searched institution, and counts "beneficiary" only when the page names it (activity-14 b); the two parts are published as one column: the relationship code, then `:` and the role code when the role is a real answer, otherwise the relationship code alone (O8); there is no separate published P06 column. The observed actor's own role is kept as a separate internal item, `observed_actor_role`, and not published (activity-15 a); the C04 grain rule is kept.

**13. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
The role field describes only the searched institution's part in the activity (contracting authority, beneficiary, central purchasing body, unit, joint) and never creates rows for another institution. Costs version steps and aligning the observed-actor relation values.

**14. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
The relationship moves to the per-activity pass; a quality check flags 'confirms activity' pages with no activity by this institution, a unit of it or a joint participant; the attribution role becomes part of the relationship, with 'beneficiary' counting only when the page names it. Test cases needed.

**15. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Relationship: this institution, unit, joint participant, other, unresolved, unknown.

**16. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Role of the searched institution: contracting authority, beneficiary, central purchasing body, unit, joint

**17. Rule** — Text you approved on 30 October
the role is asked when the relationship is `other`; skipped only when `unresolved`

**18. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
A silent page gets "not documented"; a page that mentions the matter but cannot be settled gets "unknown".

**19. Rule** — Text you approved on 30 October
Published as one column: the relationship code, then `:` and the role code when the role is a real answer (e.g. `unit_of_institution:contracting_authority`); otherwise the relationship code alone. The role is never published as a separate column.

**20. Rule (pick)** — Text you approved on 30 October
Publish relationship, then ':' and the role when the role is a real answer (e.g. `unit_of_institution:contracting_authority`); otherwise the relationship alone. Missing role labels stay internal.

**21. Long-page rule (role part)** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
the role part is taken from the same part that produced the relationship

items.body:
**1. Question** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
G3O activity typology. See definitions below.

**2. Value `policy_guidance`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Executive orders, agency memos, acceptable-use rules, procurement standards, internal guidance on permissible GenAI tools and data handling.

**3. Value `pilot_experiment`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Limited trials, sandboxes, proof-of-concept deployments, or time-bounded experiments.

**4. Value `program_initiative`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Cross-agency programs, governance bodies, training programs, or platform rollouts spanning multiple units.

**5. Value `internal_operational`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Routine internal use for drafting, summarization, knowledge search, translation, internal helpdesks, or developer tooling.

**6. Value `public_facing_service`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Citizen- or business-facing chatbots, service navigation, translation, complaint handling, case triage.

**7. Value `unknown`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Evidence confirms a GenAI activity at this institution, but the kind of undertaking is indeterminate from the available sources. Use only after the five kinds above have been considered and none is supportable -- never as a default.

**8. Rule** — Plan text, version 2.5 contract
**Rule: policy vs. pilot.** If an institution has issued a GenAI policy AND is running a pilot, these are **two distinct activities**. Produce separate rows for each (with their respective sources).

**9. Rule** — Plan text, version 2.5 contract
**Rule: country-wide program.** If a national program exists but this specific institution's participation is confirmed by a source, record it as an activity. If participation is NOT confirmed, do NOT record an activity row -- instead produce a row with `has_genai_activity` = `unclear`, `genai_evidence` = `ambiguous`, and flag `institution_attribution`.

**1. Value `deployment`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The institution puts a GenAI tool to use, or tries one out, for its own work or for the public. The stage and the purchase status are coded separately.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**2. Value `governance`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The institution issues or applies a rule on GenAI use: a policy, guidance, approved-tool list, order or standard. A body that sets or oversees such rules also counts.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**3. Value `staff_training`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The institution trains its own staff to use GenAI.
_Draft certainty: high._

**4. Value `program`** — New agent draft (round 4)

_Draft certainty: high._

**5. Value `unknown`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The page mentions the activity but does not let it be settled.
_Draft certainty: high._ _Note: The code `unknown` is also a reserved missing-answer label; template check 8 says a value code never equals one. You may want this value dropped in favour of the reserved label._

**6. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
jev Choice per activity: deployment / procurement / governance / staff_training / proposal / program / unknown. (Whether `proposal` is a type or only a stage is a PI choice.)

**7. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
Drop 'proposal' and 'procurement' from action type, since stage and procurement status carry those, and define 'program' as a container used only with named components. Your action-type choice is re-ruled and the values fixed before the version steps.

items.title: adoption stage
items.situation:
Recorded per activity.

11 slots: 7 × old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete; 3 × plan text; 1 × text you approved on 30 October.
items.body:
**1. Value `proposed`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Exploratory or hedged intent with no concrete commitment: "considering," "exploring," "studying feasibility," early discussions, unfunded or undated ideas. The text must still be explicitly generative-AI and tied to this institution. No named tool tied to a timeline, no signed MoU or contract, no budget line, no adopted policy.

**2. Value `announced`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Publicly stated intent to deploy with a concrete, documented commitment but no evidence of actual use. Includes: MoUs, budget allocations without deployment, strategy timelines.

**3. Value `pilot`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Limited deployment: subset of users/departments/use cases; described as trial/pilot/PoC/experiment; time-bounded.

**4. Value `production`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Fully operational: available to intended user base, no longer experimental, in routine operations.

**5. Value `discontinued`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Previously deployed but explicitly ended, cancelled, or suspended.

**6. Value `unknown`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Evidence confirms GenAI activity exists but stage is indeterminate.

**7. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
Keep adoption_stage for use; add `procurement_status`: none_documented / tender_or_rfp / award_or_contract / payment_or_subscription / unknown. Payment-only activities get adoption_stage `unknown` (as in the Clay fixtures) plus procurement_status `payment_or_subscription`.

**8. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
Purchase records fill the purchase-status field and get an "unknown" adoption stage unless use is shown. The owed contract amendment shrinks to removing purchase language, the procurement rules are amended, and the evidence-tier wording is fixed.

**9. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
The procurement subproject's owed §4.3 contract amendment is carried in v2.7, in the same version bumps. RC-D-002 row 27: the §4.3 amendment shrinks to removing purchase language (r2#14), and no longer waits on procurement's owed text. [wording: PI — RC-D-002 row 27: §4.3 text]

**10. Rule** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
**"Permanent pilot" rule:** If described as "pilot" but running >12 months AND serving the full intended user base, code `production`. Note in `scope_notes`: "Described as pilot but operational >12 months with full user base."

**11. Long-page rule (permanent pilot across parts)** — Text you approved on 30 October
The stage question applies the permanent-pilot rule inside each part. If the facts (over 12 months; full user base) sit in different parts, no part reaches production and the combined stage stays pilot. The codebook states this case.

items.body:
**1. Value `conversational`** — New agent draft (round 4)
Users type or speak to the tool in a chat or question-and-answer exchange, as with a chatbot or assistant window.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**2. Value `backend_or_api`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The tool runs behind the scenes, or other software calls it through a programming interface; users do not talk to it directly.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**3. Value `other_interface`** — New agent draft (round 4)
Users reach the tool in another way than a chat exchange or a back-end connection.
_Draft certainty: low._ _Note: Kept minimal: the ruling names the value only. Integrated versus standalone is carried by deployment mode (R2 n=20 b), not here._

**4. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
`interface` (one Choice): conversational / embedded_in_existing_software / standalone_application / backend_or_api / not_applicable / unknown. Functions as separate jev yes/no items (jev returns one code per question): drafting_writing, summarization, translation, search_retrieval, code, image_audio_video, extraction_classification, analysis_recommendation. Each item is chunk-safe with any-yes.

**5. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
Interface becomes conversational / back-end or API / other interface / not applicable / unknown, and deployment mode carries integrated versus standalone. This costs two version steps, regenerated questions and reference tests, a procurement copy change, and re-testing the interface question.

**6. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
The classifier chooses among the real interfaces and the missing-answer labels.

**7. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
